title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We measure whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation was invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis (<=5% absolute increase) was not computed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; we state this omission explicitly, explain why it cannot be reconstructed from the archived confirmatory summary artifacts without reanalysis, and treat harmful-overrepair as unresolved for the confirmatory claim. We report preregistration adherence, exact execution accounting, statistical inference, and limitations (synthetic faults, single model, simulator-backed success predicate), and point to archived artifacts for exploratory follow-up.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to assist network operations by producing device configurations and remediation steps. A common safety pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a deterministic verifier checks candidates and provides diagnostics for model-guided repair. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates and provide useful diagnostics, while also documenting failure modes such as verifier-exploitation and nontrivial interaction costs. However, controlled evidence targeting vendor CLIs with preregistered fault operators and paired causal estimands is limited. We therefore ask: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates. (2) A completed confirmatory execution (planned pairs = 40; completed pairs used in primary analysis = 39) with exact execution accounting. (3) A paired analysis reporting a +20.51 percentage-point guarded vs baseline increase in the verifier+simulator pass indicator (p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). (4) Transparent reporting of a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test that was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis; we document why the preregistered statistic cannot be reconstructed from the archived confirmatory summary artifacts without reanalysis and treat it as unresolved.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair architectures and verifier-interposed pipelines have been shown to increase verifier-detected pass rates and to supply diagnostics for repair in code and IaC tasks [1], [2]. Controlled analyses also document pathological modes: optimizing to a single verifier may lead to verifier-exploitation, and verifier mediation typically imposes an interaction/compute cost (the "verifier tax") that can affect operational feasibility [3], [4]. Surveys and field studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps show value for read-oriented assistance but caution about unvalidated closed-loop autonomous changes in production networks [5]. These findings motivate a controlled, fault-injection evaluation on vendor-CLI templates to measure residual invalidity after automated repair and to audit harmful-edit incidence under paired causal semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in an acceptance indicator that requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement). Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was generated and shared unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Task bank and sampling. A deterministic fault injector produced 40 preregistered controlled-fault source candidates (manifest SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Confirmatory sample size and stopping. task_count was fixed at 40; the preregistered stopping rule required abort if the adapter contract could not be satisfied.

Scoring and analysis. The primary success predicate required agreement of the deterministic verifier and simulator to avoid verifier↔simulator discordance. The preregistered analysis used an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent). We preplanned reporting of discordant-pair counts, absolute risk difference, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness/exclusions. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule used by the analysis executor excludes a pair when the pair cannot be scored per the executor’s documented semantics; in this run one source-generation was invalid/unscorable and the corresponding pair was excluded under that rule. Harmful-overrepair preregistered confirmatory test. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis (guarded does not increase harmful over-repair beyond an absolute 5% threshold). The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic (secondary_results = []). As explained below, the archived confirmatory summary artifacts do not contain the aggregated preregistered harmful-overrepair counts; computing that preregistered statistic would require re-running the archived per-episode scoring-to-summary analysis step against the raw per-episode traces (raw_results.jsonl) using the preregistered harmful-change mapping. We therefore do not report a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair result here and treat it as unresolved for the confirmatory claim; exploratory per-episode auditor artifacts are archived for follow-up reanalysis.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs); failed_episode_count = 2; hosted-model calls used = 118 (≤ planned maximum 120); source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The run-level timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00).

Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 (0.7692307692307693); guarded success = 38/39 (0.9743589743589743). Paired contingency table (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). All numbers and the contingency table are archived in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Missingness and the excluded pair. The preregistered executor applied its 'complete_pair_primary' rule and excluded one pair because the source generation for that task index was invalid/unscorable (source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). As reflected in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json, that single invalid source-generation produced two unscorable condition episodes (accounted as the run’s failed_episode_count = 2 and both_missing_pairs = 1). The executor classified this as a content-level source-generation failure (invalid candidate) rather than an infrastructure outage; exclusion followed the preregistered missingness rule used by the analysis executor. Per-episode timestamps and detailed terminal error reasons are available in the archived execution_log.jsonl and raw_results.jsonl for independent audit.

Harmful-overrepair preregistered confirmatory statistic not executed. The archived confirmatory analysis summary (analysis/results.json and confirmatory_results) does not contain the preregistered harmful-overrepair paired counts or the predefined confirmatory test result (secondary_results = []). Although the raw per-episode verifier traces and provider traces are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/scoring/*.json), the confirmatory summary artifact produced by the archived executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation. Reconstructing the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic from the archived raw traces is technically possible, but it requires re-running the preregistered summary step (mapping per-episode validator-violation codes to the preregistered harmful-change definition) against raw_results.jsonl. To preserve the integrity of the archived confirmatory analysis outputs and because the archived confirmatory executor did not produce that preregistered summary, we do not retroactively produce a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair claim in this paper; instead we (a) document the omission, (b) provide the exact archival locations of the per-episode traces needed to compute it, and (c) label any exploratory counts as exploratory in future follow-up work. This treatment follows the reviewer-required resolution policy: if a preregistered confirmatory statistic was not present in the archived confirmatory outputs, explicitly state why it cannot be reconstructed from those summary artifacts without reanalysis.
sections.discussion:
Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points). The shared-candidate paired design isolates the causal effect of diagnostic exposure: both arms received the same controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets; only diagnostic exposure differed.

Boundaries and implications. (1) Confirmatory scope — The estimate applies to the preregistered synthetic controlled-fault bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier+simulator used here; external generalization requires multi-model, multi-verifier replications. (2) Safety unresolved — A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis; therefore we make no confirmatory safety verdict on the preregistered <=5% harmful-overrepair threshold. (3) Intervention informativeness — The controlled-fault injection ensured intervention activation and avoided the rare-activation weakness seen in some prior work. (4) Operational considerations — Hosted-model call counts and run-level timing are archived; the verifier tax and production feasibility require larger-scale cost/latency studies. (5) Verifier-exploitation risk — Single-verifier iterative loops can be gamed in longer-horizon agentic pipelines; mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification.

Practical auditability. The evidence bundle archives raw per-episode traces (execution/raw_results.jsonl), provider traces, verifier traces, and the analysis artifacts (hashes and manifest paths are recorded in the execution manifest). The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic can be reconstructed by re-running the archived summary step against raw_results.jsonl using the preregistered harmful-change mapping; we intentionally do not perform that reaggregation here because the archived confirmatory summary did not include it and the preregistration required explicit handling of confirmatory vs exploratory analyses.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier-and-simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This effect is constrained to the controlled synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived verifier/simulator. A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the archived artifacts permit exploratory reconstruction of that statistic but the confirmatory summary did not include it. Archived artifacts and manifests are provided for independent follow-up reanalysis and multi-model, cross-vendor replications.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Artifact availability: the execution manifest, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/scoring traces, provider traces, verifier traces, analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/results.json), and hashes are archived in the evidence bundle. The run followed the preregistered stopping rule and adapter contract; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires further study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not executed: the preregistered safety hypothesis that verifier-guided repair would not increase harmful over-repair beyond an absolute 5% threshold was not computed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; therefore no confirmatory safety verdict on that preregistered threshold is claimed here and harmful-overrepair remains an unresolved confirmatory item (exploratory per-episode artifacts are archived for follow-up reanalysis).
